brief: A single hex base, nothing else added beside or on top of it, with five drawers in it.

requirements.requirement: A single hex base (one base piece in the build)
requirements.evidence: One Hex base · North half piece at cell 0,0,0 (role R1). The base is a half, because drawers only sit on a half base's cut face.

requirements.requirement: Five drawers set in the base
requirements.evidence: Only one drawer fits. The half base offers a single drawer socket (key s), and after it is placed no further drawer sockets appear. A full base has no cut face, so it takes no drawer at all. Five drawers would need five cut faces, which a single base does not have. The build holds one drawer (drawer:0#0,0#cut).

requirements.requirement: Nothing else added beside or on top of the base: only the base and its five drawers
requirements.evidence: Build holds only the half base and one drawer (2 parts), so nothing extra is added. The five-drawer count is not reached, so the requirement is only partly met.

finish.summary: I could not build a single base with five drawers. Drawers attach only to a half base's cut face, and a single base has one such face, so only one drawer fits. I built a North half base with one drawer and nothing else. The configurator's check is clear. R1 is met; R2 is unmet; R3 is partial because nothing extra is present but the five-drawer count is missing.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
